newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police turn water cannon on protesters.
newsitem.headline: German police turn water cannon on protesters.

text.p: Police turned water cannon on protesters outside a railway station in northern Germany on Wednesday to clear the way for a controversial shipment of nuclear waste destined for a nearby storage depot.
Germany's biggest post-war security operation reached a climax as police tried to clear a route from Dannenberg railway station to the Gorleben waste depot some 20 km (14 miles) away.
Some 30,000 police deployed to protect the nuclear waste shipment began carrying away one by one an estimated 4,000 protesters sitting on the road in front of the station.
After about four hours, they had removed only about half the demonstrators blocking a 600-metre (yard) long stretch of road directly in front of the station.

They then turned water cannon from three trucks on the demonstrators shortly after 5 a.m. (0400 GMT). Using low pressure bursts of water designed mainly to weaken their resolve and make them uncomfortable, the police continued spraying the seated demonstrators for about three hours.

Many drenched demonstrators, who tried to protect themselves with sheets of plastic and raincoats, went to the side of the road to change into dry clothing provided by other activisits and returned to the street.
Police warned the activists by loudspeaker that the action would continue unless they stopped their sit-down blockade.

The demonstrators reacted with boos and whistles but protest leaders called for calm and there were no immediate confrontations with police, although there were reports some demonstrators had shot flares at police.
The nuclear waste shipment arrived at Dannenberg in six sealed containers on a 500-metre long train from southern Germany early on Tuesday.
A convoy of flat-bed trucks was expected to begin transporting the containers of spent nuclear fuel rods to the Gorleben depot later on Wednesday.
Activists have already tried to make the roads to Gorleben unusable by damaging the surface of some, tunnelling underneath others and building barricades.
On Tuesday hundreds of masked militants lobbed fire bombs and pelted police with stones to protest against the shipment.
Two police officers were injured in the clashes and a thick cordon of police encircled about 250 demonstrators to take their fingerprints and personal details.
